texts.preamble: Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Pranav Joshi, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, New Delhi, Patiala House Courts, Delhi Ct. Cases No. 970/2022 Cnr No. Dlnd02-011726-2022 Fso Vs. Mani Kant Jha & Ors. U/S 26/51/59 Fss Act, 2006 1) The date of commission : 01.12.2020 of offence 2) The name of the complainant : Fso Naresh Kumar Sharma 3) The name & parentage of accused : 1. Sh. Mani Kant Jha, C/o M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd., Second Floor, S-20, Star City Mall, Mayur Vihar Phase I, Delhi-110091. R / o H. No. 84A, Second Floor, Munirika Village, Delhi-110067. 2. Sh. Rohit Dhingra C/o M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd., Second Floor, S-20, Star City Mall, Mayur Vihar Phase I, Delhi-110091. R/o H. No. B-53, Cr. Case No. 970/2022 Fso Vs. Mani Kant Jha & Ors. Page No. 1/12 Sector-40, Noida, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P.-201303. 3. M/s Rockers and Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88754347/ 1 Shockers Pvt. Ltd., Second Floor, S-20, Star City Mall, Mayur Vihar Phase I, Delhi-110091. 4) Offence complained of : U/s. 26/51/59 of Fss Act, 2006 5) The plea of accused : Pleaded not guilty 6) Final order : Acquittal 7) The date of such order : 13.10.2025 Date of Institution : 24.05.2022 Reserved for Judgment : 24.09.2025 Date of Decision : 13.10.2025 Judgment
texts.facts: 1. This is a complaint instituted under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'FSS Act') for violation of section 26 punishable under section 51 and 59(i) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as FSS Act). 2. Brief facts leading to filing of the present complaint are that on 01.12.2020 at about 04:20 pm, complainant, Naresh Kumar Sharma, the Food Safety Officer (FSO), had taken a sample of food article 'Paneer' by purchasing it, for analysis from Food Business Operator Sh. Mani Kant Jha from the premises of M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd., 2nd Floor, S-20, Star City Mall, Mayur Vihar Phase-1, Delhi. That the above said sample was lifted in presence of witness Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant. That after inspection of the premises, FSO showed his intention of taking a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis, where the said food article was stored for the preparation of Paneer Tikka, Chilly Paneer and Paneer Lababdar etc. for sale for human consumption, to which FBO Sh. Mani Kant Jha agreed. That the complainant purchased a sample of approx 1 Kg of 'Paneer' from an open tray bearing no label declaration. That the sample was taken after proper cutting and breaking into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean and dry steel spoon and mixed properly in a clean and dry steel bowl in which it was cut and broken. That the sample was divided into four counterparts equally immediately by putting into four clean and dry glass bottles and 20 drops of formalin was added into each sample counterpart with the help of a dropper. That each counterpart of sample was separately marked, packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 and Rules and Regulations made thereunder. That the FBO's signature were obtained on the Designated Officer's slip bearing signature of the Designated Officer, East District and wrapper of the sample counterparts in such a manner as to partly appear on the Designated Officer slip and partly on the wrapper of the samples. That FBO also obtained signatures Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88754347/ 2 of the FBO on the labels of all counter parts of the sample. 3. It is further averred that notice in Form VA was prepared at the spot and copy of the same was given to FBO. That a price of Rs. 260/- as disclosed by FBO, offered to him on account of the cost of sample, which was accepted by him. That the FBO did not prefer to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. That Panchnama and raid report was also prepared at the spot. That all the sample documents prepared by the complainant were read over and explained to FBO in Hindi and he signed the same after understanding the contents thereof. That these documents were also signed by the FBO and by the witness Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant. That one part of the aforesaid sample of 'Paneer' bearing sample number No. 335/1054/131/2020 and the Designated Officer code number 03/DO-25/16710 along with one copy of Form VI. That another copy of form VI in a separate sealed envelope having specimen seal impression was sent to the Food Analyst, Govt. of NCT of Delhi for analysis on 02.12.2020. That the FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011. That the remaining two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of form VI in a sealed packet as well as the fourth counterpart of the sample along with one form VI in a separate sealed packet were deposited with the Designated Officer, East District on 02.12.2020. 4. It is further averred that the Food Analyst vide his report number FSS/1452/2020 dated 08.12.2020 has opined that 'The sample is unsafe because it has added vegetable oil in place of milk fat, which is inferior and cheaper substance and contravenes the clause nos, (iv), (v) and (xi) of the Section 3(1) (zz) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006. The sample is also substandard because B.R. reading at 40 Deg C exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 44.0, Further, the sample contains added vegetable oil, which is prohibited and restricted for sale as per Regulation No. 2.1.1.10 of the Food Safety & Standards (Prohibition & Restriction on Sales) Regulation 2011.' That the Designated Officer, East District sent a copy of the Food Analyst report along with intimation letter dated 23.12.2020 to FBO for giving an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under section 46(4) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory (hereinafter referred to as 'RFL'), if so desired. That Food Business Operator filed an appeal under Rule 2.4.6(1) of FSS Rules, 2011 against the report of the Food Analyst before the Designated Officer, East District and accordingly one counterpart of the sample was forwarded/sent to the RFL, Ghaziabad. 5. It is further averred that the Director, RFLvide his certificate of analysis bearing certificate No. 72/Feb/21-ND dated 24.02.2021 has opined that 'The sample of Paneer does not conform to the standards laid down under Regulation No. 2.1.16 of Food Safety & Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, as the sample shows Milk Fat below the minimum prescribed limit and B. R. Reading above the maximum prescribed limit, it reveals the presence of foreign fat in it. The sample is thus substandard under section 3(1)(zx) and unsafe under section 3(1)(zz)(iv)(vi) of FSS Act, 2006.' That the instant case could not be filed before the Court within one year due to awaited reply from concerned FBO, Covid-19 Pandemic situation and large number of other case files pending with the complainant for investigation. That therefore, the Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88754347/ 3 complainant had requested for grant of extension of time limit for launching the prosecution u/s 77 of the FSS Act, 2006 in continuation from 29.11.2021 to 30.05.2022 which was granted by the Commissioner of Food Safety under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 6. It is further averred that Sh. Mani Kant Jha was the FBO-cum-Manager of M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd., at the time of taking sample and he was found conducting its business. That he was in-charge of and looked after day to day conduct of its business and liable for the offence. That M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd., is a private company having two directors namely, Sh. Rohit Dhingra and Sh. Shikhar Saxena. That M/s Rockers and Shockers has appointed Sh. Rohit Dhingra its nominee under the provisions of the FSS Act, 2006. That being a company, M/s Rockers and Shockers is also liable for the offence. That the above said accused person have violated the provisions of Section 26(1) and 26(2)(i) read with Section 3(1) (zz) (iv), (vi) of the of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and violated Section 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zx) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 2.1.16 of the Food Safety & Standards (Food Products Standards & Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 which are punishable under Section 59(i) and Section 51 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 7. It is further averred that after conclusion of the investigation, instant case file including the statutory documents along with Food Analyst report and certificate of analysis of Director, RFL was sent by Designated Officer, East District to the Commissioner (Food Safety), Department of Food Safety, Government of NCT of Delhi who accorded sanction/consent under Section 42(4)(a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 for the prosecution of accused in exercise of the powers vested in her under section 30(2)(e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and directed the complainant to institute the prosecution in the designated court of ordinary jurisdiction for the purpose of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. 8. Upon filing of the present complaint, cognizance was taken vide order dated 25.06.2022. Upon service of summons, accused appeared. After complying with the provision under section 207 Cr.P.C, vide order dated 03.06.2022, notice for the offences under section section 26(1) and 26(2)(i) read with section 3(1)(zz) (iv), (vi) of the of the FSS Act, 2006, section 26(2)(ii) read with sSection 3(1)(zx) of the FSS Act, 2006 punishable under section 59(i) and 51 of FSS Act, 2006 was served upon the accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the case was fixed for prosecution evidence. 9. The complainant/department examined FSO Sh. Naresh Kumar Sharma as PW1. He deposed on the lines of the complaint and relied upon the following documents: (a) FBO receipt Ex. PW1/A, (b) Form VA Ex. PW1/B, (c) Panchnama Ex. PW1/C, (d) Raid Report Ex. PW1/D, Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88754347/ 4 (e) Receipt of deposit with DO Ex. PW1/E (f) Report of Food Analyst Ex. PW1/F, (h) Letter to FBO Ex. PW1/G with postal receipts Ex. PW1/H, (i) Report of RFL Ex. PW 1/I, (j) Letter to FBO Ex. PW 1/J, (k) Details of nomination of M/s Rockers and Shockers Pvt. Ltd. Ex. PW1/K, (l) Sanction of Commissioner Food Safety Ex. PW1/L, The witness was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused. 10. The complainant/department examined Sh. Naubat Singh Field Assistant as PW2 who deposed similarly to PW1. The said witness was duly cross examined by Ld. Counsel for the accused. 11. The prosecution examined Sh. S.P. Singh, DO as PW3 who deposed that on 01.12.2020, he was posted as Designated Officer at Food Safety Department and on that day, on his direction FSO Naresh Kumar Sharma along-with Naubat Singh, Field Assistant went to take the sample from East district. That he signed the Raid Report Ex. PW 1/D on the next working day under Clause 4 (iii)(h) of Rule 2.1.3 of FSS Rules, 2011. That one counterpart of the sample alongwith a copy of Memo in Form VI in an intact condition in a sealed packet and another copy of Memo in Form VI in a separate sealed cover were deposited with Food Analyst on 02.12.2020 by FBO. That as the FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from NABL Accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of Food Safety and Standard Rule 2011, as such the fourth counterpart along-with the copy of memo in form VI was also deposited with him in an intact condition in a sealed packet on 02.12.2020. That all copies of memos in form VI bear his seal impression in which sample counterparts were sealed. That the Food Analyst report Ex.PW-1/F was received by him. That he intimation letter Ex. PW1/G along-with the copy of Food Analyst report to FBO Manikant Jha on 23.12.2020 for giving him an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of Food Analyst under Section 46 (4). That the accused challenged the report of food analyst and sent the counter part of the sample to RFL, Ghaziabad. That the report of director of RFL Ex.PW1/1 was received by him on 24.02.2021. That he directed FSO Naresh Kumar Sharma to investigate the case. That after completion of investigation, FSO submitted the report to him to forward for grant of sanction of Commissioner Food Safety. That he forwarded the report before Commissioner of Food Safety Ms. Neha Bansal, Commissioner of Food Safety who granted the sanction Ex. PW1/L. The witness identified the signatures of Commissioner of Food Safety. 12. Upon completion of prosecution evidence on 28.05.2025, the case was fixed for recording of statements of the accused persons under section 313 Cr.P.C. The statements of the accused persons Food Safety Officer vs Mani Kant Jha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88754347/ 5 were recorded on 29.07.2025. The accused stated that the Paneer was bought from an FSSAI approved supplier and that they do not manufacture Paneer in the restaurant. That after the incident, they had changed the vendor of the Paneer and that they had stopped buying Paneer form the said Vendor. 13. The accused initially stated that they would lead defence evidence but on 24.09.2025, on the submission of the accused, their evidence was closed. The case was thereafter, fixed for final arguments.
